activity.notes: Bayanchur Khan, also known in scholarship as Moyun Chor/Moyun Čor and by the regnal name Eletmish Bilge Qaghan, was the second qaghan of the Uyghur Khaganate. Epigraphic scholarship dates his reign to 747-759; the Tariat and Shine-Usu inscriptions preserve his reign and achievements. ATLAS uses the actual Uyghur Khaganate rather than a generic Turkic or modern Uyghur label.

sources.citation_text: Harvard Theological Review identifies Bayan Chor as the second ruler of the Uyghur Qaghanate, reigning 747-759, and credits him with transforming the polity into a major steppe empire.
